shower.thought: We spend our whole lives learning how to be ourselves, then spend the rest of it trying to be someone else.
The only time you ever truly understand someone is after they've disappointed you.
You can't remember most of your life, which means you're essentially living with a stranger who has all your passwords.
Nostalgia is just your brain playing favorites with incomplete data.
We call it "finding ourselves" when really we're just getting tired of pretending to be someone else.
The scariest part of growing up isn't realizing your parents were wrong—it's realizing why they were wrong.
You'll spend decades trying to be interesting, then realize the most interesting people are just genuinely curious about boring things.
Every conversation you have is with a version of that person that only exists in your head.
We're all just walking around with our own instruction manual that we've never read.
The people who annoy you most are usually showing you something you're afraid of becoming.
You can't prove to anyone that you exist the way you experience existing—they only get the performance.
Most of your life is spent trying to solve problems you wouldn't have if you'd just waited long enough.
Time moves slower when you're paying attention and faster when you aren't, which means you're literally losing your life by not losing track of it.
We fear being alone, but we also fear being truly known—which means we fear both loneliness and intimacy at the same time.
Your most unpopular opinion is probably the one that's closest to being true.
The people you talk to online might be the most honest version of themselves you'll ever meet.
We treat our past selves like villains when we should treat them like children who did the best they could with what they had.
Success is just failure that had better timing.
You're never really tired of a job—you're tired of the person you have to be while doing it.
The reason you procrastinate isn't always laziness; sometimes it's that you're waiting for yourself to become the kind of person who wants to do it.

darkjoke.thought:
I told my friend he was adopted.
He said, "How did you know?" I said, "Your parents actually seem happy to see you."

My therapist asked if I had suicidal thoughts.
I said, "Only on weekdays."

I went to confession and told the priest I'd been having impure thoughts.
He said, "About whom?" I said, "About you, mostly."

My dentist told me I need a root canal.
I said, "Can't you just pull the tooth?" He said, "That would be quicker and cheaper." I said, "So why didn't you suggest that?" He said, "Because I have a mortgage."

I asked my friend if he believed in the afterlife.
He said, "Not until I saw my credit card statement."

My girlfriend asked if I still find her attractive.
I said, "Of course," then immediately checked my phone. She said, "You're looking at pictures of other women." I said, "No, I'm checking the time so I know how much longer I have to stay awake."

I told my boss I needed a mental health day.
He said, "Don't you take those every day?" I said, "Exactly. I'm getting worse."

My doctor said I have a year to live.
I said, "I can't pay the bill." He said, "Then make it six months."

I asked my priest if there was any hope for me.
He said, "Have you considered other religions?"

My mom asked why I'm always so pessimistic.
I said, "Because optimists are just depressed people who haven't checked their bank account yet."

I told my date I was really into personal growth.
She said, "That's great!" I said, "Yeah, I've gained forty pounds this year."

My friend said he was getting married.
I said, "Congratulations on your first divorce."

I asked the pharmacist if these antidepressants have side effects.
He said, "Some people report feeling hopeful." I said, "That's terrifying."

My coworker asked if I was okay.
I said, "Why does everyone keep asking that?" He said, "Because you're crying." I said, "Oh, that's just my resting face."

I told my friend his new car was nice.
He said, "Thanks, it's the only thing that still responds when I call for it."

My therapist said I have commitment issues.
I said, "That's not true." She said, "We've been doing this for five years and you keep saying you'll pay next week."

I asked my date what her type was.
She said, "Tall, dark, and handsome." I said, "So I have no chance?" She said, "Not even a little one."

My friend asked if I believed in second chances.
I said, "Absolutely." He said, "Great, because I'm leaving your wife."

I told my dad I was thinking about becoming a therapist.
He said, "That makes sense—you'll finally have a captive audience."

My wife asked if I thought she was getting old.
I said, "Not at all, you look the same as the day I met you." She said, "When was that?" I said, "I honestly can't remember."
